questions.text: In which year was the founder of Buddhism born?
questions.explanation: The founder of Buddhism, Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama), was born in 563 BCE in Lumbini (present-day Nepal). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, buddhism (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is credited with founding Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Buddhism was founded by Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama), who lived in the 6th–5th century BCE in present-day Nepal/India. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, buddhism (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What significant events are commemorated by Buddhists on Vesak Day?
questions.explanation: Vesak Day commemorates all three major events: the birth, enlightenment, and death (Parinirvana) of Gautama Buddha. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, buddhism.

questions.text: The Tripitaka is the sacred scripture of which religion?
questions.explanation: The Tripitaka (meaning "Three Baskets") is the sacred scripture of Buddhism. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, buddhism.

questions.text: Which Holy Book is referred to as the New Testament in Islamic tradition?
questions.explanation: The Holy Book referred to as the New Testament in Islamic tradition is The Injeel. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, christianity (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which day is traditionally observed as the primary day of worship in Christianity?
questions.explanation: The primary day of worship in Christianity is Sunday, commemorating the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, christianity.

questions.text: Where was the first church in Christianity established?
questions.explanation: The first church in Christianity was established in Jerusalem, where the early followers of Jesus (A.S) gathered after his ascension. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, christianity.

questions.text: Who believes in the trinity?
questions.explanation: The doctrine of Trinity is a fundamental belief of Christians, who believe in God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, christianity.

questions.text: Who believes that there is no God?
questions.explanation: Atheists are those who believe that there is no God. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Zoroaster was a _?
questions.explanation: Zoroaster (Zarathustra) was the founder of Zoroastrianism, the ancient pre-Islamic religion of Persia. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study.

questions.text: Which is the second largest Religion in the World?
questions.explanation: Islam is the second largest religion in the world after Christianity, with over 1.9 billion followers. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study.

questions.text: Zoroastrian is a worship of:
questions.explanation: Zoroastrianism is a worship of Fire. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study.

questions.text: How many gods are there in Zoroastrianism?
questions.explanation: Note: Zoroastrianism worships one supreme god, Ahura Mazda, although it also has a dualist element. Zoroastrianism is a monotheistic religion that believes in one God, known as Ahura Mazda. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study.

questions.text: Jerusalem is a sacred place for
questions.explanation: Jerusalem is a sacred place for all of these — Muslims, Christians, and Jews alike. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study.

questions.text: How many gods do Sikhs believe in?
questions.explanation: Sikhs believe in One God, a monotheistic concept known as "Ik Onkar." Source: pakjobmcqs.com, comparative study (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: The Bhagavad Gita is a sacred text of which religion?
questions.explanation: The Bhagavad Gita is the sacred scripture of Hinduism. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hinduism (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What is the name of the religious scriptures of the Aryans?
questions.explanation: The religious scriptures of the Aryans are called the Vedas. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hinduism.

questions.text: What is the religion of the nation associated with Hazrat Musa (A.S.)?
questions.explanation: The religion of the nation associated with Hazrat Musa (A.S.) is Judaism. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, judaism.

questions.text: What is the meaning of the term 'Torah' in Islamic studies?
questions.explanation: The term 'Torah' (Tawrat) in Islamic studies means Law, referring to the divine scripture revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, judaism.

questions.text: To which religion does the Torah (Taurat) belong as its holy book?
questions.explanation: The Torah (Taurat) is the holy book of Judaism. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, judaism.

questions.text: What is the religious name of the Jewish temple?
questions.explanation: The Jewish place of worship is called a Synagogue. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, judaism.

questions.text: Which two religious groups consider the Dome of the Rock to be sacred?
questions.explanation: The Dome of the Rock is considered sacred by both Muslims and Jews. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, judaism.

questions.text: Talmood is a book of which religion?
questions.explanation: Talmood (Talmud) is the central religious text of Judaism. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, judaism.

questions.text: Deen e Hanif is the old name of?
questions.explanation: Deen-e-Hanif is the old name of Islam, referring to the pure monotheistic faith of Prophet Ibrahim (A.S). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous.
